findings.issue_text: 3-label sibling comparison in user_serializer.rb strips only the first label, treating a shared public suffix (e.g. co.uk) as a shared parent domain, so unrelated sites like evil.co.uk are rendered as if related

Host comparison in user_serializer.rb is case-sensitive; URI#host preserves case so mixed-case hosts (e.g. Example.com) fall through to the wrong branch and show only the host instead of the full path

Parent/child domain check is one-directional: only tests whether instance host ends with website host, so forum.example.com on an example.com instance is not handled, giving inconsistent behavior for the same domain pair
Removing the client-side computed property in user.js.es6 makes website_name a static serialized field, so the header shows a stale name after the user edits their website until a full reload
Missing test coverage for sibling-subdomain branch, mixed-case hosts, unparseable website strings, and the public-suffix collision; only exact-match, non-match, and parent-domain paths are tested
Comments in user_serializer.rb describe hosts as equal (e.g. 'www.example.com == forum.example.com') when the branches actually perform sibling and suffix checks, misstating their behavior

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 3-label sibling comparison in user_serializer.rb strips only the first label, treating a shared public suffix (e.g. co.uk) as a shared parent domain, so unrelated sites like evil.co.uk are rendered as if related

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `website_name`, the sibling-subdomain branch triggers when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and that length is `> 2`. It then compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` (i.e., it drops only the first label). For hosts like `evil.co.uk` and `good.co.uk` (both 3 labels), dropping the first label yields `co.uk` for both, so the code treats them as related and returns `website_host + path`. This incorrectly equates unrelated domains that merely share a public suffix because it doesn’t use a public-suffix/registrable-domain check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host comparison in user_serializer.rb is case-sensitive; URI#host preserves case so mixed-case hosts (e.g. Example.com) fall through to the wrong branch and show only the host instead of the full path

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the code uses `URI(website.to_s).host` and compares it directly to `Discourse.current_hostname` (and also uses it in `ends_with?` checks). Ruby’s `URI#host` does not guarantee normalization to lowercase (Ruby provides `#hostname` for a downcased host), so a user-entered URL like `http://Example.com/user` can yield `website_host == "Example.com"` while `discourse_host` is likely "example.com". That makes the equality/suffix comparisons fail and can select the wrong branch, returning only the host instead of `host + path` when the domains are effectively the same. The diff introduces this behavior and does not downcase/normalize before comparing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Parent/child domain check is one-directional: only tests whether instance host ends with website host, so forum.example.com on an example.com instance is not handled, giving inconsistent behavior for the same domain pair
Removing the client-side computed property in user.js.es6 makes website_name a static serialized field, so the header shows a stale name after the user edits their website until a full reload

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the displayed label from a client-side computed property (`websiteName` derived reactively from `model.website`) to a server-serialized field (`model.website_name`). Whether this becomes “stale after the user edits their website until a full reload” depends on update flows not shown here (e.g., whether the website edit/save endpoint returns `website_name` and whether the client updates the model with it). The diff itself does not demonstrate that `website_name` will fail to update or that only a full reload refreshes it; it only shows the field is now provided by the serializer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for sibling-subdomain branch, mixed-case hosts, unparseable website strings, and the public-suffix collision; only exact-match, non-match, and parent-domain paths are tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (exact-host match, same-length sibling subdomains, and a suffix/parent-domain check) but the new spec only exercises three cases: different domain (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact match (`example.com`), and parent-domain (`forums.example.com`). The `elsif` “sibling subdomain” branch (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is not covered, and there are no tests for case-variant hosts or invalid/unparseable `website` strings (the code rescues URI parsing to nil while `include_website_name` includes the field whenever `website.present?`). So the finding about missing coverage is verifiable from the diff, though some mentioned edge cases (e.g., public-suffix collision) are not explicitly addressed by any tests added here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comments in user_serializer.rb describe hosts as equal (e.g. 'www.example.com == forum.example.com') when the branches actually perform sibling and suffix checks, misstating their behavior

adjudication.rationale: The only issue described is that inline comments in `website_name` use examples written with `==` (e.g. `# www.example.com == forum.example.com`) while the actual code is doing base-domain/suffix comparisons rather than strict host equality. This is a potentially misleading comment, but it does not affect runtime behavior and is essentially a documentation/comment nit rather than a verifiable functional/correctness bug introduced by the diff.
